title: The Fragility Of Moral Judgment In Large Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating moral dilemma scenarios by applying content-preserving point-of-view shifts (first-person vs. third-person narration) and protocol perturbations (altering instruction placement, output ordering, and using unstructured prompts) to measure how superficial presentation changes flip model verdicts.

Injecting minimal persuasion cues into prompts (e.g., narrator self-justification, social proof, pattern admissions, and victim framing) to test if the language model unjustly alters its moral judgment to align with the user's/narrator's rhetorical stance.
